notes.zh: 作者自述：A quiet marbling bench seen from above: a shallow tray of paper-coloured water set in a dark wooden rim, lit by a soft band of morning light. On load seven drops of indigo, ox-gall, vermilion, celadon and ochre swell one after another into two sets of nested rings that press against each other, and a five-tine comb then draws itself across them, leaving feathered chevrons. The viewer keeps working the same water: every new drop shoves the existing bands outward, every drag pulls sharp feathers through them, and the fan stirs the whole surface in one slow gyre. Type stays tiny and deliberate, on a torn paper slip and a hanging vertical colophon strip stamped with the red seal of the invented Ukigumo Workshop. The tools are drawn objects resting on the wood. Pulling a print is the reward: a sheet unrolls over the water, takes the ink, turns over and flies to the drying rack, leaving a pale ghost behind for the next layer.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A dark terminal hall with one object in it: an enamel-framed Solari board for an airship aerodrome that never existed. notes.zh: 作者自述：A long-read feature from the invented magazine Crumb Quarterly, No. 14, laid out like a Sunday supplement crossed with a draughtsman's sheet: flour-coloured paper with grain and stray crumbs, a towering Didone headline with a swashed italic "of a", a drop cap, small-caps captions and monospaced measurements. notes.zh: 作者自述：A night sea in near-black ink strokes, a red-banded lighthouse on its rock, and one heavy, warm beam that is the whole game. The page opens on darkness with the title lettered across the water in tall capitals that can only be read where the slowly turning lamp falls on them. Lighting the lamp starts a four-minute night from 21:00 to 05:00: trawlers, schooners and steamers come out of the dark edges with only a lantern to show for themselves, steering for the harbour mouth, and they will avoid only the rocks the viewer has held the beam on. Everything outside the cone is guesswork and foam glints; everything inside it turns to true colour, with gold wave-crests, sparkling motes, lit sails and long shadows thrown away from the tower. Fog banks swallow the beam, a storm brings rain and swell, and at the end the sea pales to dawn and the whole reef stands revealed. Beside the sea runs the keeper's ledger, where the hour, three lanterns for remaining chances and every arrival and wreck are written in Georgia italic as they happen; the night closes on the finished log page with the keeper's own verdict on the watch.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A ten-inch ivory celluloid slide rule by the fictional makers Halloran & Voss lies on pale green-grey drafting paper, pushed in from the left before its scales engrave themselves in a left-to-right wipe and the glass cursor glides to 1. Every tick on K, A, B, CI, C, D and L is placed by logarithm, so the instrument genuinely computes: drag the slide and cursor and a strip of ruled notepaper reports the seven values under the red hairline and says in plain words what the setting works out. Index tabs on the notepaper run guided lessons in which the parts move with mechanical ease while blue pencil notes and dotted arrows write themselves on and the answer is ringed in red pencil. Below, a pencil sketch on the table restates the same setting as two hatched lengths added along a logarithmic line, next to a folded instruction leaflet that explains why it works and how to read a scale.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A loud, flat-colour Memphis-Milano landing page for an invented hot sauce made by two cousins in a bus garage. Six colour fields (yellow, pink, teal, terrazzo cream, lava red, yellow) are separated by thick black rules and scrolling marquee strips; every block is strewn with outlined squiggles, triangles, dotted circles and striped slabs that slap on like stickers and then jitter on stepped loops. The wordmark is set letter by letter, each glyph rotated, outlined and hard-shadowed, next to a squat wax-capped flask with a smiling volcano on its label. The centrepiece is a chili-shaped thermometer: dragging its little face from 1 to 10 heats the whole page (faster jitter, wobbling sweating headlines, a rattling cap, steam at the edges, colour fields flipping to red and black) until the bottle blows its cap, confetti-lava rains across the viewport, a starburst shouts "¡AY!" and the slider springs back down on its own. Trading-card sauces, sauce-able pairings, a wonky origin note and an order pad that gets rubber-stamped round it out, all in a funny bilingual voice.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white, laboratory-quiet logging sheet built around a single continuous ice core. The reader scrolls from a line-art drill tower and summit camp at the snow surface down through 800 metres of procedurally generated ice: snowy, visibly banded firn; bubbly ice; a fractured brittle zone; glass-clear clathrate ice; dusty ice-age ice; gravel-laden basal ice; and finally brown bedrock. An enormous hairline depth numeral in the margin counts every tenth of a metre against an orange reading line, with an estimated age beneath it, while annotation cards and field-log entries by Dr. Ingrid Solheim-Okafor are pinned to exact depths by leader lines that draw themselves. Three live traces, a thin-section light-box and a depth minimap stay in view; the page itself cools slightly with depth. Any point of the core can be cut: a disc slides out, turns face-on and lands in the light-box as a mosaic of crystal grains under rotating crossed polarisers, while the air released from the cut bubbles up the page.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A hushed, single-lamp mineral gallery for seven specimens that cannot exist. A brass-framed vitrine holds one real-time raymarched crystal floating above a plum velvet plinth, lit by a lamp that slowly orbits so highlights slide from facet to facet; beside it hangs an ivory museum label set in Didot-style italics with a brass catalogue number, a small property table and a paragraph of deadpan curatorial fiction, and below runs a brass rail of seven numbered crystal-habit silhouettes. The page opens in darkness and the lamp warms up over a second and a half. Changing specimen dissolves the crystal facet by facet into glints while a reflection sweeps across the case glass, then the next mineral resolves as the label re-sets itself letter by letter in glowing brass. Switching the lamp to ultraviolet drops the room into violet, makes every mineral fluoresce in a colour it has no business being, and reveals one extra line on the label written in fluorescent ink.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, full-bleed garden pond seen from directly above at midday. The water runs from pale jade shallows at the mossy corner stones through teal to a deep centre, with pebbles on the floor and a slow net of caustic light sliding over everything, fish included. Nine to thirteen koi, each a flexing spine with its own painted pattern (kohaku, showa, ogon, tancho), cruise in bursts and glides, paddle their pectoral fins and drag soft shadows across the floor that lengthen over deeper water. Lily pads drift on tethers, two lotus flowers breathe, maple leaves turn, water striders dart, and now and then a dragonfly and its shadow cross the frame. The page opens in white glare that settles like eyes adjusting to the sun while the fish swim in from the edges. There is nothing to achieve: tap for ripples, hold to feed, and watch the whole pond turn towards one spot.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white-cube gallery reduced to two values. The visitor arrives at a title wall where enormous condensed capitals are sliced by horizontal hairlines that beat against each other, then walks down through six snap-aligned rooms that alternate between black and white. Each room holds one square work made from nothing but a repeated line, ring, check or spoke laid over a copy of itself: rings that produce sweeping hyperbolas, a checkerboard that swells into a dome, upright stripes that ripple, spokes that bloom into counter-rotating petals, ruled paper that folds into a pleated curtain, and finally a black disc that the viewer stares at until it disappears and leaves a glowing ghost on a blank wall. Signage is tiny, uppercase and widely spaced, with a large roman numeral and a dry wall note per room. The mood is exacting, quiet and slightly dizzying; everything that seems soft, grey or three-dimensional is produced by the viewer's own vision.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A clock that is only a sentence. The viewer's local time is written out in lowercase English and set as a wood-type broadside: every line is measured to its ink and scaled to the full width of the screen, the minute phrase in heavy italic, the whole block packed into a solid rectangle on a single flat field of colour that drifts through twenty-four hand-picked pairs across the day, from aubergine small hours through dawn peach, white-hot noon and terracotta evening back to deep blue. When the minute turns the poster re-typesets itself in place: only the letters that differ roll out and in, and the lines swell or shrink to stay flush with both margins. In the corners, tracked monospace capitals carry the date, year, time zone and day of the year, all in words, while a hairline along the bottom edge counts the seconds. The effect is of a printed sheet that happens to be alive, calm at rest and briefly mechanical once a minute.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A wide marsh sky in the last minutes of light: plum-ink overhead sinking through mauve and coral to a pale apricot horizon, a low sun and its broken reflection in a thin strip of water, pylons and poplars tiny on the far bank, and a black reed bed swaying along the bottom edge. Into the empty sky a long ribbon of starlings streams from the right and gathers into a single breathing shape made of thousands of tiny flapping chevrons, lighter where the birds are far and darker where the flock folds over itself, stretching into ribbons and hourglasses and rippling with sudden dark waves when it turns. The viewer's pointer is a peregrine; the flock parts around it, wraps behind it and closes again, and a click sends the falcon into a tucked dive that tears a hole straight through the birds. Left alone, the falcon hunts by itself, the light slowly fails, and the whole flock drains through a narrow neck into the reeds; after a few seconds of stillness a new evening begins. The only words are a tiny italic title, a live count of starlings, a hint that dissolves once the hunt starts, and two quiet controls.

tags: - Boids simulation in typed arrays with a counting-sort uniform spatial grid; separation, alignment and cohesion limited to about seven sampled neighbours - Per-cell sums for a wider neighbourhood heading, centre-of-mass pull and a density-gradient pressure that keeps the flock a spread fabric rather than a clump - Twin roost attractors that drift on slow Lissajous paths and periodically separate, pulling the flock into ribbons and hourglasses - Excitable-medium agitation wave (delay, attenuation, refractory period) passed between neighbours, drawn as briefly thicker, longer strokes - Fake depth from a per-bird z blended with a moving sheet field; four depth bands by stroke width and opacity, each split into calm and agitated batches - Birds as two-stroke chevrons whose wings alternate in length to flap; batched Canvas 2D strokes - Low-resolution density buffer from the grid, bilinearly upscaled as a soft smoke-like shadow where the flock overlaps itself - Procedural dusk painting: four-stop sky gradient, translucent horizontal washes, sun bloom and disc, mirrored water gradient with a broken sun reflection and animated glints, value-noise treeline, lattice pylons with sagging wires, poplars, vignette and baked grain - Long thin clouds built from stretched radial gradients on their own layer, drifting by compositor transform - Two-layer reed bed with quadratic-curve stems, plumes, bulrush heads and leaves swaying on layered sine waves, stirred locally where birds land or erupt - Falcon silhouette drawn from quadratic curves with banking, wingbeat and a tucked stoop pose, plus stoop streak and expanding ring - Evening state machine: slow light fade, funnel descent with a fanning neck, rest, new evening - Adaptive quality (flock size, reed and haze refresh rate), DPR cap, pause when hidden, reduced-motion variant - Web Audio wing rush: looped noise through band-pass and high-pass filters with a flutter LFO, driven by flock speed and fear

notes.zh: 作者自述：A top-down view of a classroom demonstration: a sheet of warm white paper, fibres catching soft daylight, dusted with fourteen thousand black iron slivers. Two red-and-blue bar magnets glide in from opposite edges and the random dust visibly combs itself into the textbook pattern, pulling a dense bridge of filings across the gap between north and south. From there it is a toy: slide, spin and flip the magnets and watch the alignment wave chase them, see tufts of filings cling to the poles and get dragged along leaving swept trails, flick the paper to tidy the lines, bring like poles together to find the pencil-circled null point, and drop a horseshoe or disc magnet, a compass, or a fresh shake of filings from the apparatus tray. A taped typewritten label and a pencilled note are the only words on the sheet.

tags: - Two stacked Canvas 2D layers: a procedurally painted paper (fibre strokes, noise tooth, daylight wash, vignette, printed registration marks and scale bar) and a live layer - Filing simulation in typed arrays: summed softened-monopole field, per-filing lagged axis alignment, gradient-of-field-strength creeping with friction and per-filing stopping thresholds - Batched line rendering in six paths bucketed by dithered field strength and grey variation, with length and weight tied to field strength - Magnets, compass and shaker drawn in code with painted-metal gradients, stamped lettering, bevel highlights and lift-dependent drop shadows - Flip animation by axis scaling with polarity swap at the midpoint and the field strength following the turn - Damped-spring compass needle driven by the local field - Midpoint-integrated streamlines seeded around each pole with arrowheads and a progressive draw-in, in pencil blue - Automatic null-point detection between like poles with a hand-drawn pencil annotation - Outward-travelling tap ring that jitters filings as it passes - Time-based tweens with custom easing for the entrance, tray hand-offs and tray/label choreography in CSS - Web Audio noise hiss mapped to filing motion, off by default - Sleep-when-settled render loop, DPR cap, resize rescaling, reduced-motion variant

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white sheet set like a Swiss mathematics poster: an enormous lowercase grotesk headline runs up the left edge with one word in red-orange, a hairline-framed square field fills the height of the window, and a narrow monospace rail of rules, sliders and tabular figures sits to its right. The field holds every integer up to N as one small square. It opens by drawing all of them as a single black line, reeling that line into a solid black square spiral, and then sieving it from the centre outward behind a red front until only the primes remain, scattered along unmistakable diagonals. Choosing another arrangement sends every dot along its own path, centre first, so the square coils into the Sacks spiral, flares into the polar galaxy, or falls into rows whose columns stripe at widths like 30 and 210. Pointing at any dot produces a black label with its arithmetic and lights the diagonal, curve, column or arm it belongs to in red; zooming in far enough turns the dots into numbered tiles.

tags: - Sieve of Eratosthenes with prefix tables (prime count, twin pairs, widest gap) computed once in typed arrays - Direct pixel plotting of up to 250,000 squares into a Uint32 view of canvas ImageData, with culling and DPR capped at 2 - Per-point staggered morphing with a tabulated cubic-bezier(.65,0,.2,1) ease; unwrapped polar interpolation between the Ulam and Sacks spirals, shortest-arc polar interpolation to and from the (n, n) plot, Cartesian elsewhere - Opening choreography: progressive line draw, wrap into the spiral, radial red sieve front with a grey trailing band - Vector overlays on the same canvas: twin-prime links, Euler's polynomial thread with filled/hollow markers, the highlighted quadratic or residue class, a sprung cursor ring with tick marks - Level-of-detail numerals drawn inside each square once cells are large enough - Anchored exponential zoom smoothing so the point under the cursor stays put - Rotated vertical headline in tight bold grotesk with clip-path wipe entrance; rules that draw in along the rail - Custom sliders, square toggles, inverted radio rows and a live gap histogram built from plain elements - Cross-fade via a snapshot canvas for reduced motion

notes.zh: 作者自述：A slow, bilingual landing page for the invented Parisian house Maison Ombre and its single fragrance, No. 7 — Bibliothèque Brûlée. On warm ivory laid paper, crossed by a drifting casement of pale window-light, an enormous oxblood italic title runs behind one exquisitely drawn flask; the word seen through the glass is bent by it, and the amber-oxblood liquid inside tilts, sloshes, ripples and bubbles as the pointer passes or the flask is tipped. Scrolling carries the same flask into the olfactory pyramid, where its oak cap lifts off and the notes rise from the neck as fine wisps and then evaporate in order, top first, heart next, base lingering, before three quieter movements: a portrait of the perfumer beside a scorched, tea-ringed folio, the object's specifications with a dimensioned elevation and a discreet table of editions, and a one-line request for a sample card that is answered by an envelope closed with a wax seal.

tags: - Flask drawn entirely in inline SVG: eight bevel facets, layered linear gradients for thick glass, gilt collar, charred-oak cap with grain and cracks, paper label with old-style numeral - Liquid surface rebuilt every frame from a spring-damped tilt angle plus a one-dimensional wave simulation that reflects off the walls; a second offset line gives the surface depth - Bubbles spawned by slosh energy that rise, wobble and dimple the surface when they break - Refracted title: a live copy of the second title line clipped to the flask cavity, magnified and offset about the cavity centre and re-registered each frame - Blurred SVG cast shadow and wavering caustic streaks under the flask that lean and brighten with the position of the window-light - Window-light as a skewed, blurred grid of six panes drifting on a slow sine; glass reflections shift with it - Laid-paper texture from two repeating CSS gradients (laid lines and chain lines) - Wisps as pooled SVG paths whose points are advected through a slow sinusoidal flow field, coloured gold, oxblood and soft black for top, heart and base - Scroll-driven choreography with smoothed scroll position and smoothstep easing: flask travel and scale, cap lift, note emergence, tracking and evaporation, hour clock - Title entrance by true letter-spacing closing from wide to set, with per-letter staggered opacity - Scorched folio using feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap for torn edges and cockled lines, a radial scorch gradient and a broken tea ring - Dimensioned line elevation that draws itself with stroke-dashoffset; hairline rules that draw in from the left - Wax seal with turbulence-displaced edge, radial gradients and an embossed SVG monogram, dropped and pressed with spring-like keyframes - Custom gold ring cursor that follows on a spring and swells over interactive elements - Reduced-motion version with a level, still liquid, all notes visible, no wisps and a fixed window-light

notes.zh: 作者自述：A single cathode-ray tube sits in a dark cabinet above an engraved model plate. Everything on its face is light: mint-white beam cores wrapped in green bloom, vertices that burn a little brighter where the beam pauses, and a phosphor that takes a moment to forget what it was shown. The attract screen traces the word DESCENT one stroke at a time while a cratered wireframe moon turns behind it and an autopilot quietly demonstrates a landing below. Starting a mission hands over a small legged module drifting above jagged regolith; the camera eases in to two and a half times scale as the surface approaches, the engine plume fans out and flickers, dust streaks away along the ground in short glowing lines, and the whole tube brightens with the burn. A clean touchdown earns a dry remark from mission control and a harder site; anything else scatters the lander into its component segments, which tumble, bounce and fade while the phosphor remembers their arcs.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A six-spread stapled zine laid out on a cutting mat, printed in exactly two inks. Everything on the page, from the full-width cover title to the smallest weather icon, exists twice: once on a fluorescent pink plate and once on a teal plate, multiplied together over flecked recycled paper so that overlaps turn a deep violet nobody paid for. The plates never quite agree. As the viewer moves, scrolls or tilts, the pink plate slides a few pixels against the teal one with a soft spring, keylines drift off their fills, halftone screens beat against each other, and a printer's registration target in the corner reports the error and can be dragged to make it much worse or double-clicked to make it, briefly, perfect. Inside that process sits a warm, funny little publication by two damp people and a cat: instructions for taking a spore print (with a cap you can lift to watch one land), five mushrooms described like neighbours, a centrefold of roots and mycelium growing under the fold, letters, a month of rain, and a stamp telling you to pass it on.

tags: - Two stacked SVG plates per illustration (pink and teal) composited with mix-blend-mode: multiply over paper, so overprint produces the third colour - Global registration offset driven by CSS custom properties, added to a different base error on each spread, with spring-damped motion - Ink grain: tiling SVG feTurbulence tiles (fine speckle multiplied by coarse mottling) used as CSS mask images, different for each ink - Recycled paper: thresholded turbulence flecks and stretched-noise fibres as tiled backgrounds - Halftone dot screens and line screens as SVG patterns at different angles per ink (15° and 75° dots, crossed line screens) - Hand-drawn wobble from an feDisplacementMap filter applied identically to both plates - Radial gills drawn with a single dashed, very wide circle stroke squashed into an ellipse - Cover title as SVG text with textLength fitting, pink flat plus teal keyline with screens clipped to the letterforms - HTML headlines doubled with pseudo-elements: pink fill on the moving plate, teal text-stroke keyline on the fixed plate - Canvas spore print: thousands of jittered dots along primary, secondary and tertiary gill rays, revealed from the centre outward - Procedural centrefold: seeded random-walk roots with tapering widths, mycelium links and wandering forks, grown with stroke-dashoffset; rebuilt in portrait proportions on phones - Paste-up blocks with torn tape, crop marks, colour bar, drawn staples and fold shading, scribbled page-number rings - Container-query units so each spread scales like a printed sheet; paper-slap entrance with an overshooting cubic-bezier

title.zh: Plotter No. 2 — Landscapes in One Pen
title.en: Plotter No. 2 — Landscapes in One Pen

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, technical bench-top scene: a white A4 sheet lies on a pale grey gridded cutting mat inside a drawn pen plotter with two aluminium rails, a travelling gantry bar, a black carriage with a cable loop and a ballpoint whose red clip is the only warm colour besides the hold button. On load the carriage homes into the corner with a small bump, rules the border and registration crosses, then works through the sky, each ridge from far to near, the lake or pines, and finally letters its own title block. The landscape is a true plot file: every mark on the sheet is an ordered polyline that the pen actually travels, with travel moves, pen lifts, corner slow-downs and ink that is paler when the pen runs fast. The pleasure is in watching tone accumulate as the machine hatches a mountainside in hundreds of quick strokes, while a small LCD reports pen state, coordinates, percentage and time remaining, and a listing on the mat ticks off the layers. Every new sheet is a new seeded composition, and the finished ones pile up in the out tray.

tags: - Seeded procedural landscape: 5–8 ridgelines from layered value noise and ridged noise with a peak envelope - Hidden-line removal with a running per-x horizon, walked front to back, also used to occlude the sun, clouds and the ridges behind the pines - Five hatching generators (slope-wobbling contours, vertical rain dashes, cast-shadow cross-hatching, scree stipple, downhill fall lines) with density falling off with distance - Lake of horizontal dashes whose density mirrors the skyline through a ripple displacement; pines as dense zigzag strokes - Single-stroke vector alphabet defined in the page, used for the plotted title block - Path simplification and greedy nearest-endpoint ordering of each layer to minimise pen-up travel - Motion planner: resampled paths, corner speed limits, forward/backward acceleration passes, trapezoidal travel moves - Incremental ink rendering on an offscreen canvas at capped device pixel ratio: pen-down blobs, speed-dependent opacity, width jitter and minute positional wobble - Canvas-drawn machine: brushed aluminium gradients, steppers, gantry trucks, a sprung cable loop, pen shadow that separates on lift, servo arm and state lamp - CSS-built control panel: brushed faceplate, conic-gradient knurled dial, lever toggle, keycaps, emergency-stop style hold button, reflective LCD with segment bar - Sheet feed animation with eased slide, slight rotation into a peeking stack of earlier plots - Optional stepper sound: two oscillators pitched from the X and Y axis speeds, filtered noise clicks for pen up and down

title.zh: Rhythmus — A Drum Machine in Primary Colours
title.en: Rhythmus — A Drum Machine in Primary Colours

notes.zh: 作者自述：Rhythmus is a poster that happens to be an instrument. On warm, toothy paper a wall of hand-drawn geometric capitals climbs the left edge, and a heavy black bar cuts across the sheet at seventeen degrees with the tempo reversed out of it like a ruler. Six flat-colour shapes balance on and hang from that bar: a blue circle resting on the incline, a red square standing on its edge, a yellow triangle, a black half-disc facing its outlined twin, a thin red mallet on a black pivot, a blue ring. Below, a six-by-sixteen grid repeats the same shapes in miniature as the score. Press the red circle and the composition starts to move: every drum hit is performed by its shape with spring physics, the playhead sweeps the grid, the title letters step along with the bar, and the whole print keeps time. Everything is drawn in code, with slightly ragged printed edges and off-register fills, and the layout re-composes for phones with the stage above a two-page grid.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A silent winter night at 69°N, seen from the shore of an invented fjord. The page opens on stars, black mountains and one lit cabin window; then a green curtain of light unrolls from the left and the sky comes alive. Three aurora curtains hang in true perspective: folded ribbons with crisp, bright lower borders, tall rays that shimmer sideways, pale cores and violet upper fringes, the nearest arching overhead while the farthest lies low over the mouth of the sound. Snow on the peaks picks up the green, the water below breaks the whole sky into long trembling streaks, and a thread of smoke rises from the cabin beside a jetty and a moored boat. A small plate of type in the corner names the place and slowly turns the pages of an observer's notebook. The viewer can simply watch, or stir the solar wind and call down a substorm that floods the fjord with light.

Snow on the peaks picks up the green, the water below breaks the whole sky into long trembling streaks, and a thread of smoke rises from the cabin beside a jetty and a moored boat. A small plate of type in the corner names the place and slowly turns the pages of an observer's notebook. The viewer can simply watch, or stir the solar wind and call down a substorm that floods the fjord with light.

title.zh: Drawer 31 — Moths That Were Never Caught
title.en: Drawer 31 — Moths That Were Never Caught

notes.zh: 作者自述：A walnut specimen drawer slides out from under a cabinet rail and fills, moth by moth, with two dozen species that never existed: emperors with ringed eyespots, swept hawk-moths with rose underwings, angular lichen-green geometers, stout owlets and tiny fringed micros, each painted procedurally from a seed, mirrored for symmetry and then slightly damaged the way real specimens are. Rows are grouped under printed genus headers, every pin in a row sits on one line, and beneath each moth is a small tilted label in uneven sepia handwriting. The lining paper is foxed at the corners, the glass carries a faint moving reflection, and the drawer front holds a brass label holder, a cup pull and a small brass switch. To one side a huge Didot numeral and a dry curatorial note explain the collection of E. M. Hollis, who pinned the moths he was sure of and never caught. The experience is quiet and studious: pass a brass magnifier over a specimen to read its scales at three times life size while its typed index card slides out, turn the whole drawer over to see the pale undersides, pull the next drawer, and eventually discover that one specimen in each drawer is still alive.

notes.zh: 作者自述：The viewer stands inside the lift car of the Hotel Meridian, a sixty-storey Art Deco hotel of 1931, and scrolling is riding. The screen is fixed: two brushed-brass doors engraved with chevrons and a rising sunburst, a semicircular brass floor indicator above them, verdigris wall panels either side, a strip of veined black marble underfoot. As the page scrolls the indicator hand springs from floor to floor, shaft lines streak through the gap between the doors, and at ten floors the car stops, sways, and the doors slide apart on a small flat Deco scene with one looping motion each: a revolving door, a spinning globe, waltzing silhouettes under a mirror ball, a swinging bulb on bare brick, parrots on perches, dripping lost umbrellas, a cake being iced at 3 a.m., a lone swimmer under the moon, a tram crossing below a telescope, and finally the roof with the hotel's neon sign seen backwards against the dawn. Each scene is captioned in the dry, discreet voice of the attendant, Mr. Abernathy. The mood is luxurious, nocturnal and slightly haunted; the whole page is lit by brass against lacquer black.

title.zh: Side A — A Turntable in CSS
title.en: Side A — A Turntable in CSS

notes.zh: 作者自述：A catalogue-style spread for an invented 1974 turntable, the Marlowe PL·7, playing an invented jazz LP, "Slow Weather" by the Marguerite Okonkwo Quintet. A walnut plinth with a cream deck plate sits tilted in real perspective under a translucent sage dust cover, in front of a burnt-orange supergraphic sun and sage shelf stripes; a fat italic "Side A" headline, a sleeve note, a leaning record sleeve and a track list sit to the left, and a brushed-aluminium amplifier with two VU meters and a pair of walnut speakers complete the system. Everything is drawn from HTML elements and gradients and everything moves without a line of script.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A parish census drawn as a single sheet of cream paper: on the left, a small masthead and seven questions set as large serif sentences; on the right, one enormous numeral, a phrase that completes it, and three hundred coloured dots that are, each of them, somebody. The dots rain in and settle into a packed cluster of households; ask another question and every family lifts off together, arcs across the page and springs into place as a population pyramid, nineteen clusters of occupation, a hand-ruled map of six streets under a hill, a beeswarm of arrival years, a choir on its risers above a grey audience, or a ring of friendships. The headline counts to its new value, the rules and labels draw themselves in, and a sentence written from the data sits underneath, dry and affectionate. Hovering any dot produces a little card with a name, an age and a one-line life; pinning it lets you follow one person through every statistic they belong to.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A quiet potter's studio on a single screen: linen wall with a patch of window light, a bench with a dusty blue water bucket and two spare balls of clay, and in the middle a charcoal splash pan with 900 g of wet terracotta turning on the wheel head. The page opens with the lump wobbling into centre and a pair of ghost fingers opening it and making one pull, so the clay rises in the first seconds; then the viewer takes over and the wall follows their fingers, getting taller as it is collared, squatter as it is bellied, thinner as it is pulled, and folding into a heap if it is rushed. Around the wheel the type is set like a craft catalogue: small-caps labels, potter's notes in tiny italic numerals, a hand-drawn tool rack and one large italic line, "Centre. Open. Pull. Breathe.", whose words light in turn. Wiring the pot off begins the second act: it is lifted on tongs, dipped into a bucket of glaze, watched through a glowing kiln peephole while the cones bend and the counter climbs to 1,240 °C, and comes out glossy to slide onto a wooden shelf that fills up over the session.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A cold room at 2 a.m., seen as one full-bleed window: four panes in a dark wooden frame, a sodium-lit street dissolved into heptagonal bokeh behind them, and frost drawing itself across the glass in real time. The first ferns shoot out of the lower-left corner, then everything slows to a patient creep: curved plumes with herringbone side branches at sixty degrees, six-armed frost flowers, lines of ice running along invisible scratches, all stopping where they meet older ice so the pane fills over about two minutes yet keeps clear islands. Where the ice is dense the street behind turns pale and diffuse, and crystals glint when a lamp or a passing car's headlights slide behind them. Hold a finger to the glass and a haze of breath blooms, the frost melts outward into beads, a few drops run down leaving clear tracks, and when you let go the patch quietly freezes over again with ferns that were never there before. The only words are "breathe here", fingertip-written in old condensation and already half frozen, a thermometer on the frame, and a tiny caption on the sill.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A fine-press book of five pages on warm paper, in blue-black ink with one red mark per page. The cover sets "Five" in italic over an enormous "Calligrams." and types its subtitle onto a pale wave. Each page then performs its poem: Rain falls in slanted columns of words that splash letter by letter at the ground and part around one red, dry "umbrella"; River carries a long sentence down a meander, letters springing at the source, swelling where two small tributary sentences run into it; Heron stands as a bird made of type and, when ready, lunges its neck of words at the water as "not yet" becomes "now"; Stair lets the reader's scroll bounce a red full stop down seventeen word-steps to the floor; Breath opens and closes a ring of words at four seconds in and six out. Any poem can be un-shaped into plain stanzas and shaped again, so the reader can watch form become, and stop being, meaning.

title.en: Conservas Maré Alta — Tinned Fish Since 1923

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunny, proud landing page for the invented cannery Conservas Maré Alta of Porto Salgado, drawn entirely as mid-century tinned-fish packaging: flat inks in cream, tomato red, sea teal, sun yellow and navy, halftone-dot shadows, off-register outlines, arched banners and numerals in ovals. A red hero patterned with tiny fish carries the headline "The sea, kept." beside an oversized, tilted tin whose wrapper comes alive (sunrays turning, a sardine leaping with a splash beside a striped lighthouse). notes.zh: 作者自述：A wall of Victorian instruments mounted on grained mahogany: a great aneroid barometer at the centre, ringed by an anemometer, a 32-point wind rose, a psychrometer, a rain gauge, a clockwork barograph in a glazed case, a sunshine recorder and a cluster of small dials for tide, sea and visibility, all under a brass plaque. Nothing is a number in a box; every value is a needle, a mercury column, a water level or an ink line. A week of invented weather runs on a fast clock, and a deep Atlantic low arrives a few seconds after the page opens: the barometer needle sinks heavily into the red sector, the vane backs and twitches, the anemometer surges with each gust, rain streaks cross the window reflected in every glass, the light dims, and a red storm cone climbs the signal mast while the observer's log writes its warning in a slanting hand. Then the front goes through, the vane flies round to the north-west, and the glass leaps. The experience is meant to be calm and exact, like standing in a quiet room while the weather happens outside.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, paper-coloured tangram table in the manner of a mid-century picture book. Seven flat-coloured wooden pieces begin as the classic square, burst apart into a loose scatter, and a pale dotted silhouette draws itself onto the work mat. A lettered caption reports the time, and a vermilion stamp is pressed into a row of eight.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A Halden Portable, Model 5, sits on a lamp-lit wooden desk in 1958. A sheet of warm paper rises out of its black rubber platen and fills the upper part of the view; below it are the grey-green enamel deck with its fan of steel type bars, two ribbon spools, a nickel nameplate, a strike counter, and a bank of round glass-topped keys. The machine types its own first line with a human rhythm, returns the carriage, and then waits with a pulsing red caret at the printing point. From there every key the viewer presses is a physical event: the key sinks, a type bar leaps from the basket, the ribbon jumps, the paper shudders, an imperfect inked letter lands and settles, and the whole carriage steps one space to the left. Nothing can be erased, only struck over. Finished sheets are pulled out and drift onto a fanned pile that can be read again.

tags: - Per-glyph ink synthesis on a 2D canvas: each character is drawn to an offscreen stamp with a fill plus a heavier outline, then cut by a randomly offset alpha mask combining low-frequency blotch noise, a diagonal ribbon-weave pattern and dropout specks, and multiplied onto the sheet so overstrikes darken - Persistent per-slug misalignment (every character has its own fixed offset and tilt; notes.zh: 作者自述：A flat, saturated tangerine living-room wall carries a supergraphic of seven concentric stripes that sweeps in from the left edge and bends down around a single rocket-shaped lava lamp standing on the edge of a teak sideboard. The lamp's spun-aluminium cap and hourglass base frame a tapered glass vessel in which glossy magenta wax lifts off a settled mound, stretches, necks to a thread, pinches in two, cools at the top and sinks again, all in amber liquid with drifting sparkle, a specular streak and a small window reflected on the glass. Fat cream Cooper-style lettering with a stepped aubergine drop-shade sits low on the wall beside it, over a quiet lowercase caption that says "wait for it." until a blob lets go. The page opens cold: the stripes draw themselves, the title springs up, the bulb flickers on, its glow spreads up the wall and the first big blob leaves the mound. The mood is warm, drowsy and unapologetically 1971.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A white-cube gallery rendered as a long page: an entrance wall with the museum's name in enormous tight black grotesque under a single blue waveform that dies away into a flat line, then nine exhibit rows, each with a huge outlined catalogue number, a single-weight line drawing standing on a plinth, and a wall label written in a dry curatorial voice. The front face of every plinth is an instrument panel: a round blue button, an oscilloscope and a small spectrogram that show the sound actually being made at that moment. Nothing is recorded; a rotary dial, a modem handshake, a typewriter, a television, a camera, a floppy drive, a cassette, a slide projector and the time pips are all built from oscillators, filtered noise and envelopes, and each drawing performs one exact mechanical movement in step with its sound. The modem is the centrepiece: its plinth panel widens across the whole row and a large spectrogram writes itself out while brackets caption the conversation between the two machines. A mechanical tally counts what has been heard, and the exit wall keeps its last label in storage until all nine have played.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A fixed sky above a stubble field outside the invented village of Ellery, where a small crowd, two tripods, a dog and a single ash tree wait for a total eclipse. Scrolling is time: the Moon bites into a pale warm Sun, the blue sky thins to steel and then to twilight indigo, the field drains to silver, shadows harden, and an inset shows the ground under the tree covered in crescent suns. In the last minute shadow bands ripple over the field, the umbra rises from the west, the crescent breaks into Baily's beads along a jagged lunar limb and collapses into a diamond ring with bloom and diffraction spikes. Then the page goes dark: a delicate, asymmetric, shimmering corona unfurls around a black Moon, pink prominences cling to the limb, Venus and stars appear, the horizon glows orange all the way round, rooks fly to roost, the dog howls, and the word TOTALITY breathes across the sky above the quiet line "Two minutes, eleven seconds." Scrolling on plays it all in reverse on the opposite limb until daylight, colour and an ordinary afternoon return and people pack up. A clock, a contact timeline, a thermometer that falls six degrees and a needle light meter keep the facts while sparse second-person annotations keep the feeling.

tags: - One fixed full-viewport 2D canvas (DPR capped at 2) redrawn from a single eased scroll-progress value; everything is reversible - Real eclipse geometry: circle-intersection area drives the light level, sky keyframes, land colour, shadow sharpness and readouts - Sky built from four interpolated six-stop gradients (day blue, steel, indigo, totality with a sunset-orange horizon band) - Procedural corona: polar texture of noise-modulated rays, tapering equatorial streamers and fanning polar plumes, tone-mapped and pre-rendered to two offscreen buffers that are cross-faded, slightly counter-rotated and radially masked to unfurl - Fixed jagged lunar limb profile (720 samples) used both to draw the Moon and to compute which valleys still pass sunlight, producing Baily's beads and the final diamond - Diamond ring with additive bloom sprite, eight tapered diffraction spikes, soft halo ring and lens ghosts along the optical axis - Pink prominences and chromosphere arc drawn on the Sun's limb and uncovered asymmetrically by the Moon's motion - Landscape of layered hills, village with spire, furrowed field, ash tree and a crowd of silhouettes whose colours desaturate toward silver and fall to black against the horizon glow - Radial-gradient shadows whose penumbra narrows as the Sun becomes a sliver; wavy moving shadow bands clipped to the field; umbra as a growing dark radial wall from the west - "Look down" inset: 280 pinhole images stamped from a live crescent sprite matching the current phase, inverted as a pinhole would - Twinkling stars, labelled planets, a flock of flapping birds crossing the orange band, a howling dog with drifting letters - DOM typography over the canvas: Georgia annotations with small-caps time stamps, thin wide-tracked sans for TOTALITY with per-letter breathing spacing, ink colour that switches with sky and field luminance - SVG needle light meter, thermometer readout, vertical contact timeline with live clock; notes.zh: 作者自述：The page is four folded cyanotype sheets from the drawing office of a one-woman frame shop in an invented Calder-valley town. Sheet 1 opens by drafting a fully dimensioned side elevation of a lugged steel touring frame, fork, wheels and a dotted rider under a headline lettered across the whole width of the sheet, with a schedule of dimensions and a pencilled margin note from the builder. Sheet 2 hands the viewer four scale rules; moving any of them recalculates a real frame geometry and the drawing redraws itself tube by tube, numbers rolling and flashing marking-out yellow, construction arcs swinging through the tube ends, the rider leaning further forward or sitting up, the wheels shrinking to 650B for short legs, while every change is logged as a lettered revision that also updates the drawing number in each title block. Sheet 3 shows three circular detail views of the joinery with numbered balloons and the builder's reasons in her own hand. Sheet 4 sets out fourteen weeks of work as a hatched bar chart, plain prices, an apologetic waiting list, and a request form that carries the viewer's figures and ends with a yellow RECEIVED stamp slammed onto the title block. Everything is line work in four colours on blotchy blue paper with fold creases, masked borders and zone marks.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A museum-cabinet instrument on sunlit plaster: a dark walnut frame carries a row of brass bobs on fine strings, their lengths cut so that each makes one more swing per minute than its neighbour. A hinged release bar holds them to one side, lifts, and the row leaves in unison, then slides into a travelling wave, tangles, sorts itself into four, three and two interleaved groups, and at exactly sixty seconds sweeps back into one line while a brass ring spreads from the frame and the dial glows. Beneath the frame the same row is seen from above as a single undulating line with a fading wake; at the side a brass-bezelled sixty-second dial names the pattern of the moment and states the arithmetic behind it; along the bottom a brass rule lets the viewer slide to any instant. Everything is computed from the closed-form angle, so any moment can be visited exactly and the minute repeats forever without drift.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunlit blush tabletop with a cream toy-like instant camera called the dawdle, its teal neck strap looped off to the side, a small box of film, and eight dashed outlines waiting for pictures. Pressing the red shutter fires a white flash, the iris blinks, the camera kicks, and a square print is pushed out of the slot in motor steps, drops free and glides to its numbered place at a slight tilt. There it stays milky grey-green and then, over twelve seconds, shadows surface first, warm tones follow, and finally a handwritten caption appears on the border. Each of the eight frames is a tiny flat illustration in a faded-film palette: a striped parasol, a cat's back at a window, a boiled egg with steaming coffee, a caravan under pines, a bicycle, a lighthouse with a breathing beam, a cake with flickering candles, two feet at the end of a towel. The counter runs from 8 to 0, the shutter goes grey under an "empty" tag, and a sticker on the film box loads a fresh pack. There is not a line of script on the page.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A complete broadsheet front page for an invented port city, printed in ink black on yellowing newsprint: a blackletter nameplate with an engraved harbour vignette, weather and price ears, a ruled dateline, and seven columns of period journalism about a great fog, a new electric tramway, an escaped circus sea-lion, a police court, a serial story, shipping, sport and small advertisements whose details quietly refer to one another. notes.zh: 作者自述：A single sheet from an imagined eighteenth-century astronomical atlas, lit as if by a candle: laid paper with chain lines, grain and foxing, a border of tiny asterisks, and a title cartouche set in mixed capitals, small caps and italic. At its centre sits an embossed plate-mark holding a graduated degree circle, an engraved radiant Sun, and two small planets circling at their true relative speeds. Every few days a hair-fine line is ruled between them and left behind; within three seconds the first petal appears, and over eight simulated years the tangle resolves into the five-petalled rose of the 13 : 8 near-resonance. When the cycle closes a red flourish draws itself under the caption, asterisks mark the five conjunction points, and the caption states plainly how far the figure misses closure. Left alone, the next eight years are then ruled slowly in madder red over the first, a hair askew. The viewer can change pace, weave density and view, scrub through time, and swap in five other planetary pairs, each with its ratio and loop count worked out from the same twelve numbers. A short two-column essay insists, calmly, that it is all only division.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A weathered slab of slate lies on dark ground, lit from the upper left, with a hairline crack, stepped cleavage and two rust veins. Three lichen colonies are already growing on it when the page opens: a mustard crust branching into coral lobes, a sage shield lichen unrolling broad leafy lobes, and a chalk-white crust budding at its edge. They grow slowly but visibly, with pale young margins, raised relief and soft shadows; their centres age, darken, crack and break out in tiny dark-rimmed fruiting discs. When colonies meet they stop and hold a thin black frontier, and over a century the slab turns into a map of territories. A pinned field card in a typewriter face and italic hand records the year and each species' share of the stone; a specimen tray offers four species to sow; a brass hand lens follows the pointer and magnifies the crust two and a half times. The mood is quiet, damp and northern.

notes.zh: 作者自述：The page is the decorated surface of an Attic black-figure drinking cup: a terracotta ground with clay grain, wheel marks, hairline cracks and a chipped rim, black glaze bands carrying the title in spaced, slightly uneven cream capitals, a Greek-key meander above and below, a running-wave band, and two palmettes flanking a round tondo. Inside the tondo is a freshly generated ring labyrinth. A small black silhouette of Theseus steps in at the gate paying out an oxide-red thread that lies along the corridor floors with a little slack; Asterion sleeps in the central chamber under his own name. Reaching him wakes him, the meanders begin to scroll, and the way out is the thread itself, rewound step by step while the Minotaur pathfinds behind, stopping to sniff at junctions. Escape sends the whole thread springing back along the remembered route, pulling taut, lifting off the pot and winding into a ball on the cream roundel beside the title while the vessel makes one slow turn and a cream slip panel delivers the inscription.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A long-scroll specimen for Halden Grotesk, an invented geometric grotesk from the invented foundry Nordre Type, in which no font file exists: all 35 glyphs are stored in the page as explicit on-curve and off-curve points and drawn from that data. The page is clinical and Scandinavian: specimen-paper off-white, black, and a single cobalt used for construction lines, points and one giant letter, organised on a twelve-column grid with hairline rules and mono section numbers. The cover crops an enormous "Halden" at the viewport edges and assembles it from points, outline and a rising flood of ink. Anatomy pins one glyph out on a metrics grid with every coordinate labelled and every point draggable; because that drawing is the master, damaging the "a" damages every "a" on the page until it is reset. Construction shows the compass work behind O, G and D and an eight-times vertical exaggeration of the overshoot; In use sets a waterfall, a weight row, a poster and ferry-terminal signage from the drawn letters only; Spacing lets the viewer kern a pair by hand until it snaps to the foundry's value; the Colophon carries the designer's note, a licensing joke and the full character grid with its gaps.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A single woodblock print hangs on a pale wall and quietly lives. An arched timber bridge runs in a long diagonal from a snowbank and its reeds to a far shore of thatched and tiled houses, a stone lantern and two cinnabar gate posts, under one snow-capped mountain that dissolves into the sky. Everything is cut as a printer would cut it: flat colour blocks with woodgrain showing through, hand-wiped bokashi at the top of the sky and along the water's edge, dark indigo keyblock lines whose width breathes, colour sitting a hair out of register, and snow that is simply unprinted paper. On arrival the sheet is pulled block by block (sky, water, greys, red, key lines), the cartouche settles and the two artist seals are stamped last. Then snow falls in three depths, wave lines drift down the river, a figure in a straw cape under a red umbrella crosses the bridge with a dog or a lantern-bearer behind, chimney smoke curls, crows pass now and then, a roof sheds its load. The hour follows the viewer's clock; pressing the round seal re-inks the sky from the top down, and at dusk the windows and lanterns come on one after another, their light laid on the river as short warm strokes. On phones the scene recomposes as a tall oban sheet; on wide screens it is a diptych.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A jeweller's-black landing page whose hero is a working watch. The Heure Bleue 38 lies caseback-up beside a large Didone title: under the sapphire, a ruthenium-dark calibre with rose-gold wheels is actually running, every wheel meshing at its true ratio and the whole train stepping six times a second to the viewer's own local time. In the first three seconds the crown turns three clicks, the ratchet advances, the blued mainspring tightens in the barrel, and the balance kicks into life. Turning the watch over reveals a restrained ivory dial with applied gold indices, blued leaf hands, small seconds at six and a moon-shaped power reserve; everything on both faces is annotated in French and English on hover or tap. Below, four sparse sections ruled in thin gold give the specifications, the two-person workshop, three finishing close-ups that respond to light, and a waiting list whose confirmation is engraved letter by letter onto a caseback ring.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunlit natural-history gallery wall in shell-pink plaster. A large porcelain-white shell floats above a linen-covered drum that stands on a pale cabinet of eight brass-labelled drawers; beside it hang a paper museum label and a brass-and-ivory instrument of five sliders and two rows of small specimen trays. On arrival a chambered nautilus grows out of its own apex, whorl after whorl, flame stripes and all. Pulling a drawer makes that shell become another before the visitor's eyes: the flat coil tightens and telescopes into a turret, swells into a cone shell tiled with computed tents, or flares open into a ribbed cockle valve, while the label re-sets itself, the slider handles slide to their new places and a crosshair travels across the map of all possible shells below. Sawing the nautilus open reveals a spiral of pearly chambers. The tone is quiet scholarship: classical serif titles, tracked small-cap legends, plain accurate copy about why a shell that grows only at its edge must be a logarithmic spiral, and how David Raup found that life uses only part of the space the equation allows.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sideways journey down an invented English river, drawn as one continuous flat-colour panorama in the manner of a children's atlas for grown-ups. The page opens in rain on a moor, with the title lettered large in rough-edged Palatino italic and a paper boat dropping into a spring no wider than a pencil line. Scrolling carries the reader 138 kilometres downstream: over a gritstone fall, under a packhorse bridge, past a turning mill wheel, through buttercup meadows, a terraced brewery town, a working lock, pylons and poplars, mudflats, docks, and finally past a lighthouse into an evening sea. The river is a single unbroken blue path that widens from a thread to the whole lower third of the stage, and the little boat rides it the entire way, behaving differently at every obstacle. Each of the eleven stations carries a white-on-green kilometre sign and a short, dry caption; a slim strip along the bottom shows the whole river in miniature with an altitude profile and a live readout of distance, height and flow.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A black acrylic desk toy fills the viewport: a glossy rounded frame slung between two chrome posts, holding roughly ten thousand hexagonally packed steel pin-heads (about five thousand on a phone). On arrival a hand presses in from behind and withdraws, and its impression slowly melts back into the lattice. Every pin is a tiny domed, lathe-turned disc lit by a single raking lamp, so slopes facing the light flash white, slopes facing away drop to dark steel and raised forms throw shadows across their lower neighbours. The pointer itself becomes a hand pushing through the field; dragging leaves a subsiding trail. A tray of machined black keys presses in a hand, a mask-like face, a sphere, a travelling ripple, a typed word and the current time, and a flip key tips the frame so the whole field cascades out and back in a glittering wave. The only colour anywhere is one thin red line on the brushed-steel logo plate, which states the true pin count.

tags: - WebGL point-sprite renderer: one point per pin, round heads cut and antialiased in the fragment shader, with a Canvas 2D fallback using pre-rendered disc sprites in 16 brightness levels - Per-fragment lighting on each pin-head: surface normal from the neighbouring pin heights plus a small dome, diffuse and tight specular terms, a bow-tie "turned steel" glint aimed at the lamp, darkened chamfer rim, per-pin brightness variance - Height-field gradients computed on the hexagonal lattice by least squares over the six neighbours; cast shadows found by marching four steps toward the lamp - Height-dependent parallax and 15% growth of raised heads, with a perspective-varying parallax vector so the field reads as slightly tilted - Steel tone ramp restricted to #0B0C0E, #6C7480, #C9CED6 and #FFFFFF, plus a lamp-centred sheen falloff across the flat lattice - Spring-and-gravity pin physics in typed arrays: fast underdamped spring when pushed, slow friction-limited relaxation with slightly randomised rates when released, bouncing free-fall during the flip - Procedural height maps: capsule-and-ellipsoid hand, ellipsoid mask face, sphere, animated concentric wave, and text rasterised offscreen then box-blurred per pin - CSS-built object: acrylic frame with lamp-tracked gloss, chrome cylinder posts with knurled caps and pivots, brushed-steel plate with slotted screws, floor glow, film grain - Frame swing on a hand-written spring driving a 3D rotateX under perspective - Inline SVG icons for the tray, lamp and hint; tracked small-caps geometric sans typography - Synthesised sound: a looped buffer of thousands of tiny decaying noise ticks through two band-pass filters, gain driven by the summed pin velocity - Idle detection (nothing is simulated or redrawn when the field is at rest), DPR capped at 2, frame-time measurement that thins the lattice on slow machines

title.zh: BÉTON BRUT — Six Buildings Nobody Asked For
title.en: BÉTON BRUT — Six Buildings Nobody Asked For

notes.zh: 作者自述：A photocopied architecture zine, issue six of BÉTON BRUT, laid out as nine full-viewport spreads on a board-marked concrete-grey ground. Colossal condensed capitals crop at the page edges and run behind six isometric concrete models of an invented new town, Northmere; typewritten essays by the zine-maker Dot Ferreira sit on taped-down pale slips with orange marginal numbering. As each spread arrives its building is poured storey by storey out of the base plate, flashing orange formwork as each lift sets, then the giant name slams in behind it, the page shakes and a rubber stamp lands. Every model can be turned, pulled apart into a labelled section and re-lit with a sun slider that throws a long shadow across the page. A charcoal manifesto spread and a back cover with a creased fold-out site plan and a cut-out subscription coupon close the issue. The tone is monumental, argumentative, affectionate and a bit funny.

tags: - Isometric models built from divs with CSS 3D transforms (preserve-3d, orthographic rotateX/rotateY rig): extruded boxes, many-sided drums, tilted folded plates with clipped gables, a 50-segment helical ramp - Per-face lighting computed from a sun vector: each face normal is dotted with the light direction and mapped onto a pale-cement to charcoal concrete ramp, with orange details shaded on their own ramp - Projected ground shadows: every volume's corners are projected along the sun vector onto the base plate, convex-hulled and drawn as one SVG path lying in the ground plane - Pour choreography with individual scale/translate properties, cubic-bezier(.7,0,.2,1), 250–400 ms lifts staggered by level, and a keyframed orange formwork outline that sets to concrete - Board-marked concrete from layered repeating gradients (plank lines, knots, tie-hole grids), water stains and moss as blurred gradient streaks, SVG turbulence grain - Photocopier grit: an SVG turbulence alpha mask punching toner dropouts into the giant type, page numerals and rubber stamps - Window modules drawn with tiled conic gradients so one face carries a whole grid of openings - Overprint: orange type and the cover sun set to multiply over charcoal letters - Billboarded scale figures, section labels and plan markers that counter-rotate to face the viewer inside the 3D rig - Fallback-font fitting: canvas text measurement drives a horizontal squeeze so any heavy grotesque matches the condensed display width - Crop marks, taped paper slips with hard offset shadows, fold creases on the site plan, dashed coupon border with SVG scissors, hand-drawn SVG signature that writes itself

notes.zh: 作者自述：A living four-colour screenprint. A cream sheet carries a giant stacked "sand / pile" title with misregistered orange and blue shadows, and the dot of its "i" is itself a seven-by-seven sandpile that never stops toppling. Beside it a large square table with a black outline and a hard shadow sits empty for half a second, then a tap opens over the centre and a fractal medallion of ink, orange and blue blooms outward behind a ragged yellow front before settling into a slow drip. Everything else on the sheet is a readout of that one rule: a looping four-panel pictogram, a legend whose bars and counts follow the table, a tally in tabular numerals, and a log-log plot whose orange points drop into place along a blue fitted line as random rain is measured. The viewer pours, pins taps, drops handfuls of ten thousand grains, computes the group identity, sweeps the table with a diagonal wipe and saves the result as a poster.

title.zh: Seven Sisters — A Nest of Dolls
title.en: Seven Sisters — A Nest of Dolls

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sheet of cream paper with a folk-painted shelf across its lower third, a slowly turning floral rosette behind it, and one lacquered nesting doll standing in the middle. Tap her at the waist and her top half springs up, tips and is set down leaning on the shelf, a dark wooden hollow appears, and the next sister rises out of it, hops over the rim, lands with a squash and a wobble, and gets her name ribbon; the row slides to stay centred as the family grows. Six times this repeats, each sister smaller by a fifth and painted with her own scarf, face and apron motif (sunflower, strawberries, rooster, samovar, rowan, tulip), until Little Zoya, who is solid and asleep. Tapping Zoya wakes her: her eyes open, she blushes and jumps, the painted bird leaves her apron, grows as it climbs and circles above the sisters, and seventeen flowers bloom one by one along the bottom border. All of it runs without a single line of script.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A working observatory instrument presented as a page of stationery: an engraved masthead, a slate-and-brass elevation drawing of the seismograph (clockwork gearbox with a stepping escapement, a paper-wrapped drum sliding along its lead screw, long boom, knife-edge pivot, oil damper, sprung mass) and beneath it the unrolled recording sheet, where a simulated pen draws a continuous trace line by line. The page opens with the pen dropping onto the drum in the decaying surface waves of a distant earthquake, whose P, S and L flags, distance, magnitude nomogram, telegram and ledger entry appear as the first seconds pass. Everything the visitor does to the page (knocking, shaking, striking the pier with the mallet) is recorded by the same damped pen, annotated in red ink on the sheet and entered in the ledger with a dry remark. Analog readouts, a rack of filed sheets and a framed notice complete the bench.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A lamplit, velvet-dark room with one object in it: a bottle-green enamelled Holloway & Stern safe with gilt pinstriping, three brass hinges, a five-spoke handle and a large combination dial. After a filament flicker the lamp comes on and the dial gives one idle spin to zero. The viewer cracks a random three-number combination by intimacy with the mechanism rather than by reading a display: every graduation clicks, but the gate of the wheel being worked sounds lower, softer and doubled, the dial drags for an instant, the red index shivers and the needle of a small stethoscope gauge leaps. A notepad quietly pencils in each number when the viewer rests on it. Throwing the handle on a wrong setting gets a clunk and a shudder; on the right one the three bolts thud back one by one, the handle spins, and the heavy door swings open in true perspective, showing its thickness and boltwork, onto felt shelves holding one of five small stories: a pearl, a bundle of letters, a ship in a bottle, a sleeping cat, or a card that says "Too late. — M."

notes.zh: 作者自述：A grey, overcast landing page for a fifth-generation umbrella maker on which it is actually raining: several hundred simulated drops fall in three depth layers across the whole viewport, splash on the top edges of the paper panels and the pavement, and blur and drain the colour from everything they fall on. The viewer holds the only bright thing on the page, a canary-yellow umbrella drawn in quarter view, which replaces the cursor. Rain bursts on its canopy, beads slide down the panels to the rib tips and fall in a steady drip, and beneath it a soft circle of the page is dry: sharp, full-contrast, and in colour. Reading the page means sheltering it. The copy is dry in the other sense: a headline that says it is raining in Garrow and usually is, an exploded drawing of the Garrow No. 4 that assembles itself when scrolled into view, a house catalogue of eleven grades of rain, a ruled price list for repairs, the shop's hours ("closed on dry days, i.e. the 3rd of August"), a note from Odalys Pluvia, and a footer wordmark standing at the edge of a puddle that reflects it upside-down and ripples when drops land.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sheet of green-bar fan-fold listing paper steps up out of a dark platen, a print head sweeps a JCL job banner and a huge "#" banner title across it, and then the rest of the sheet prints a seascape that will not hold still: a horizon, cloud wisps, a lighthouse on its rock, a little sailing boat, a bell buoy and a beach, every one of them made of typewriter characters and recomputed each frame from a perspective wave field in two ribbon colours, black for faces, crests and foam and sea-green for deep water. Moving the pointer is the weather: down for a glassy calm with mirror reflections, up for a gale with towering slashes, slanting rain, inverted-sheet lightning and a typed thunderclap, sideways for the wind. Whatever the viewer types falls from the sky into the water and rides the swell as a legible sentence, each letter on its own column of the wave, until it washes up as a tide line of their words. A footer in the voice of a shipping forecast for "Greenbar Bight" reprints itself in place as conditions change.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A quiet nocturnal instrument: one cratered Moon hanging in a sparse field of fixed stars on night black, shown at the phase it has at this very minute. Beneath it the phase name is set in very large, light serif type, followed by one italic line of copy written for that phase and a single ruled row of tabular data (illumination, age, date and time). A small column lists the next four principal phases, with the coming full moon in harvest gold; along the bottom edge a tape of day-by-day moon glyphs slides under a fixed index, today ringed in gold. Dragging the tape sweeps the terminator across real relief: crater rims catch the light, floors fill with shadow, the old Moon in earthshine appears around new, and every readout ticks along. The page opens in darkness, the lit limb arrives as a hairline, the light sweeps to the true phase and the title letters settle into place.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A full-bleed painted landscape in gold and slate: two-thirds of the screen is a field of ripe wheat receding to a hazy horizon of hills, hedgerow trees, a spire and a lone oak, under stacked flat-shaded storm clouds with a cream sun-break and light shafts. After one still beat a gust enters from the left and the whole field comes alive: every stalk is its own spring, leaning and overshooting as bands of wind sweep through in perspective, turning the crop silver-pale where it bends and dark just ahead, so the wind itself becomes visible as waves rolling away. In the foreground, individual ears with paired grains and trembling awns nod above olive grass, a few poppies and cornflowers; swallows scatter from a telegraph wire when a gust reaches them and a kite circles. Over four minutes a dark bank slides in, the light narrows, the caption counts down, heavy drops streak and spot the wheat, thunder mutters, and the weather eases back into bright wind to begin again. The experience is meant to feel like standing at a field margin, expectant and tender, with the option of putting a hand out into the wheat.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A history-of-science vitrine with the glass taken away. A large engraved brass astrolabe lies on a lamplit parchment table beside a column of museum text headed by the cinnabar exhibit number IV.12 and the invitation "Please touch." The instrument is lowered onto the table, its shackle swings, and the rete makes one slow turn before stopping at the present hour with the rule laid through the Sun's bead, so that at rest it is already telling the time. Every circle on it is real stereographic geometry for the chosen latitude, and a label-card panel reads the instrument back in plain language as the visitor turns it: the Sun's place in the zodiac, its height, the hour under the rule, the degree rising and the degree culminating. Three numbered tasks teach sunrise, day length and culmination step by step, ticking themselves off as the visitor succeeds. On request the whole instrument separates into a calm axonometric stack of pin, horse, rule, rete, plate and mater, each named and explained, and then settles back together.

title.zh: Par Avion — The Journey of One Letter
title.en: Par Avion — The Journey of One Letter

notes.zh: 作者自述：A single airmail envelope sits at the centre of a kraft-paper stage and never leaves it. As the viewer scrolls, nine flat, duotone postal scenes conveyor past behind it — a rain-streaked pillar box, a cancelling machine, the pigeonholes of a night mail train, an aerodrome, a desert stopover, a flying boat, a colonial G.P.O. counter, a mail boat and a cliff-road bicycle, a schoolhouse — while a top ribbon traces the route on an invented map and a ticker runs the local date and time. The envelope is the travelogue: each stage physically strikes, sticks, stains or creases it, with handstamps that drop in, thump and lift away leaving patchy, slightly doubled ink that dries from wet to matte. Captions on airmail-edged cards speak in the dry voice of a public-information film. At the end the envelope turns over, a paper-knife opens it, and the letter it has been carrying the whole way unfolds: a brother writing to his sister about rain, a ship's cat, an honest kettle and their mother's knee. Scrolling back up un-stamps every mark and sends the letter home.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, clinical lab-manual page built around a living ripple tank. A framed tray of pale aqua water sits on a white bench with corner screws, legs and an apparatus shelf beneath it; numbered experiment tabs run across the top like headings in a practical handbook, and a side column carries the experiment note, one live formula, the frequency control and the probe plot. The page opens on the double slit: a plane wave marches from a red bar, strikes a lab-blue wall, and two fans of wavelets cross into alternating beams of glittering crests and calm nodal lanes, while red hand-drawn arrows name the central maximum and a nodal line and the plot beside the tank grows a row of fringes under thin red prediction ticks. Everything in the tank can be dragged, rotated, resized or thrown out, so each textbook diagram can be bent into another one.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A magazine long-read from the invented quarterly "The Lee Shore" whose weather is its subject. The page opens almost blank: an amber harbour lamp glows at the end of a silhouetted mole, the letters of the huge wide-tracked title condense out of the mist one by one, and then a slow, volumetric fog settles into its drift between the reader and the essay. Text is always dark slate ink underneath; the fog is thick in the top and bottom of the window and thin in a reading band across the middle, so paragraphs come into legibility as they are scrolled to the centre and thin away again. Each of the five sections has its own weather: a light sea-fret for the vocabulary, a dense smoor for the foghorn, a near-total blanket for 1952, and a clear, sharp morning for the close. A fixed "Visibility" readout names the current conditions, the foghorn sends an amber ring through the fog every ninety seconds of story-time, and a "Lift the fog" control clears everything for anyone who simply wants to read.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunny one-button arcade game set at the counter of the invented Gelateria Belmonte. A waffle cone stands in a mint holder on a marble counter beneath a blue-and-cream striped awning whose valance is lettered "Torre di Gelato"; between two pastel seaside houses lies a sliver of sea with a sailboat, a promenade railing and a gull. A server's striped sleeve swings a spade overhead, and each tap drops a soft scoop that squashes, ruffles, sticks and makes the whole tower lean, sway and overcorrect, every scoop jiggling a beat behind the one below. Dawdle and the sun melts the lower scoops into drips that run down the cone and pool on the marble. As the tower climbs, the camera leaves the awning behind and rises past washing lines, rooftop cats and aerials, a bell tower whose clock shows the viewer's own time, gulls, a kite, a hot-air balloon, thin clouds, a banner plane, a crescent moon, stars and a small satellite, each with a dashed height marker. Three dropped scoops end the round with a slow, messy cascade onto the counter and a paper receipt listing every flavour in order, with a total and a dry verdict from Signora Belmonte.

title.zh: Strange Attractors — A Collection of Orbits
title.en: Strange Attractors — A Collection of Orbits

notes.zh: 作者自述：A dark viridian vitrine holds one strange attractor at a time, built from up to 480,000 points of gold dust whose overlapping density, not any drawn line, makes the form: thin outer loops are faint threads, the folded cores glow champagne, and a jade shadow of the same density lies on a graduated floor ring beneath. The page is composed like a museum label on glass: a large Didone name and plate number at top left, the governing equations set in italic serif with live, draggable constants at bottom left, a row of seven miniature specimens at bottom right. The experience is slow and tactile: the specimen turns on its own until taken in hand, a swarm of bright tracers shows which way the flow runs and how quickly neighbours part, and every change of plate or constant makes the whole cloud dissolve and re-settle into its new shape rather than cut.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunny mid-century instructional poster that is also a working instrument. A flat, geometric sailor stands on a signal deck with a rail, a lifebuoy, a coil of rope, the sea horizon, a steamer and one small cloud, holding two diagonally divided red-and-yellow flags. Type a message onto an invented naval message form (S.1320, with TO / FROM / TIME boxes and ruled typewriter lines), press SEND, and the signaller spells it out in correct flag semaphore: arms snapping the shortest way round an eight-point clock with a slight wind-up and overshoot, flags folding edge-on through the move and cracking open with follow-through, the body leaning and bobbing with each position, rests between words, a quick drop between double letters, and the numerals and letters-follow signs inserted automatically. A strip of tiny static glyphs lights up in red in step with the performance while the current character stands beside the figure in huge stencil type. On load the signaller calls attention with both flags and spells HELLO unasked. A second tab turns the page into a reading trainer with a streak counter and a ship's bell, and a reference chart of thirty positions, grouped by the seven circles of the code, lets the viewer play the signaller like an instrument by hovering, tapping or pressing letter keys. Everything is shown as seen by the observer, and says so.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A sunlit, nearly monochrome amber landing page for a nine-hive honey producer, built from one material and one shape. A turned beech dipper lowers into the top of the page and lets go of a single thread of honey that falls through the oversized serif headline and coils like a rope onto the first cell of a full-bleed honeycomb. Scrolling makes the comb fill outward from that landing point: each cell rises with a curved meniscus, then most are sealed with a dimpled wax cap while some stay open and glossy. Three seven-cell clearings in the comb hold the three honeys with their hexagonal jars. Bees patrol the cell walls, fly off in arcs and drift toward a resting cursor. Below the comb everything remains hexagonal: a twelve-cell ring calendar, interlocking number cells, a compass and a dance floor for the waggle dance, and an order cell that ends in a pressed wax seal. The voice is first person plural, dry and fond of its bees.
