notes.zh: 作者自述：Lumen is a municipal power dashboard built as a model-railway board: an isometric pastel town of some thirty buildings on a steel-blue plinth, with a wind ridge, a sun field, a weir, a battery barn and a pylon line to the mainland, all wired to a tiny substation. One simulation of a 24-hour day drives both the model and the instruments around it. The board opens empty, buildings spring up district by district, wires string themselves between poles, and yellow dashes begin to run along them at a speed and density that match the kilowatts on each line. As dusk falls the board tints from cream through pink to a dim lavender, windows light house by house, the Bijou's marquee comes on, the wind drops, and the viewer watches the battery barn's flow turn round and the interconnector start importing. Around the model sit a day dial, frequency gauge, segmented battery, a 24-hour stacked supply chart with the demand line, today's mix ring, a carbon-free streak, the mainland account in pounds and a dryly written event log, all in the same flat navy-outlined style.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A darkened Victorian parlour: a brass wall lamp flares up at the upper left, throwing a warm pool over patterned wallpaper and a mahogany table on which stands a slotted drum on a turned pedestal. One automatic flick sets it spinning, and within three seconds the bright slits sliding across the near wall fuse into a cream band in which a row of small black-and-vermilion horses gallops on the spot, dimmer and narrower than the drawings on the paper band lying unrolled on the table in front. As the drum coasts down the figure flickers, breaks into sweeping bars with comet tails of drawing, and finally stands as twelve separate slivers. Nothing is faked: the picture is built each frame by sampling the far-wall strip through the moving slits into a persistence buffer that fades like the eye, so the speed, direction and failure of the illusion all follow from how the viewer spins the drum. A reading glass on a stand shows the central figure enlarged; lifting the slotted lid turns the same drawings into a grey smear; and a drawer in the table holds twelve blank frames for a strip of the viewer's own.

notes.zh: 作者自述：A bright, sunlit aquarium tank in which the Collatz conjecture is a living plant. The reverse tree of every path from 1 to 9,000 grows out of a sea-urchin "1" on a sandy floor: thick deep-teal trunks through 2, 4, 8 and 16, thinning and paling into thousands of sea-green hairline fronds that lean and curl because even steps bend one way and odd steps the other. The whole forest sways in a slow travelling swell while garibaldi-orange and teal fish weave through it, bubbles rise and marine snow drifts. The page is set like a museum panel: a bold serif title and three plain sentences in the upper left with the rule drawn as a two-branch sprig, a cream instrument plate with a number field, famous starters and two brass dive-gauge dials, a specimen card with the hailstone plot, and a strip of statistics printed on the sand ending in "counter-examples found: 0". The signature moment is following a number home: one orange thread lighting the whole way down through the forest to 1.

title.zh: Gemini 4 重构 Chromium 大型代码库
title.en: Applying Gemini 4 for large-scale codebase maintenance in Chromium

notes.zh:
演示什么：Chromium 的代码库有数百万行、积累了几十年；Google 工程师 Erik Chen 用 Gemini 4 Argon 让多个 agent 并行拆解架构、改代码，再由 Chromium 的测试套件与人工代码评审把关。
官方怎么说：视频把重点放在「多个 agent 独立工作、测试与评审兜底」，不是一次生成整库。
边界：这是 Google 内部案例，不是受控基准；视频没有给出提交量、失败率、回滚率或与其他模型的同题对比，不能当作「Argon 能独立维护任意代码库」的证明。
notes.en:
What it shows: Chromium’s codebase is millions of lines and decades old; Google engineer Erik Chen uses Gemini 4 Argon to let multiple agents untangle the architecture and change code, with Chromium’s test suites and human code review as gates.
What the official video says: the emphasis is on multiple agents working independently with tests and review as backstops, not one-shot generation of the whole repository.
Boundary: this is an internal Google case study, not a controlled benchmark; the video does not give commit volume, failure rate, rollback rate or a same-task comparison with other models, so it is not proof that Argon can maintain any codebase alone.

title.zh: Gemini 4 教人形机器人投沙包
title.en: Teaching a humanoid robot to play cornhole with Gemini 4 Argon

notes.zh:
演示什么：Google DeepMind 的机器人团队让 Gemini 4 Argon 看一段人投沙包的视频，模型在 MuJoCo 里搭出虚拟仿真，算出物理与全身控制参数，再交给 Apptronik 的 Apollo 2 人形机器人执行；官方称它在真实世界连续投进 7 球。
官方怎么说：这条 Video-to-Sim-to-Real 流水线把「几周的手工建模」压到「几小时」，目标是让普通视频变成物理 AI 的训练场。
边界：这是内部测试的单个任务，不是跨任务成功率；视频没有给出尝试次数、失败分布、 sim-to-real 偏差或安全边界，不能外推成「人形机器人已通用」。
notes.en:
What it shows: Google DeepMind robotics researchers had Gemini 4 Argon watch a video of a person playing cornhole; the model built a MuJoCo simulation, calculated the physics and whole-body control, and handed them to Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid, which the official video says sank seven consecutive shots in the real world.
What the official video says: this Video-to-Sim-to-Real pipeline compresses weeks of manual modelling into hours, turning ordinary videos into a training ground for physical AI.
Boundary: this is a single internal test task, not a cross-task success rate; the video gives no attempt count, failure distribution, sim-to-real gap or safety envelope, so it does not generalise to “humanoids are solved”.

title.zh: Gemini 4 Argon：10 个官方演示，100 万 token 输出

notes.zh:
演示什么：Google Cloud Tech 用 40 分钟串起 10 个官方演示，覆盖 1960 年代 Fortran 迁移到 Rust/C++、Android UI 自动构建、WebGPU 实时毛发、3D 数据可视化、NASA Artemis II 轨迹、从餐巾纸草图到 3D 打印硬件等。
官方怎么说：团队称投入 1,000 多小时实测，核心卖点是 Argon 的 100 万 token 输出上限与长程推理，能一次交付大体量、可验证的结果。
边界：这是精选演示合集，不是同题横评；成功案例被选出展示，失败与成本没有逐项披露，不能把「10 个都能跑」当成平均能力。
notes.en:
What it shows: Google Cloud Tech spends forty minutes on ten official demos, spanning 1960s Fortran migration to Rust/C++, autonomous Android UI construction, real-time WebGPU fur, 3D data visualisation, NASA Artemis II trajectories and a napkin sketch turned into 3D-printed hardware.
What the official video says: the team reports 1,000+ hours of hands-on testing and frames Argon’s 1M-token output ceiling plus long-horizon reasoning as the ability to deliver large, verifiable results in one run.
Boundary: this is a curated showcase, not a same-task comparison; successful cases were selected for display and failures/costs are not disclosed item by item, so “all ten ran” is not an average-capability claim.

notes.en:
What it shows: Google’s official article lists eight use cases: interactive tools and playable 3D games, lifelike textures, real-time 3D rendering, physics simulation and music visualisation. One example has Argon in Antigravity orchestrate subagents, Blender MCP and Nano Banana to turn photos of a real desk into a playable 3D track.
What the official article says: it stresses Argon’s grasp of real-time 3D, lighting, shading and interactive physics, plus the ability to chain tools into one agent pipeline.
Boundary: this is an official use-case gallery, not an independent evaluation; it does not give each example’s prompt, project files or failure rate, and some assets involve other models such as Nano Banana, so not every result belongs to Argon alone.
